39.t:
He was the eldest of his brothers and the last of them to die, and he was the grandfather of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, the hadith scholar (المحدث).
He had sons: Muslim, Yazīd by whom he was given his patronymic (الكنية), Saʿīd, Jaʿfar, Abū Saʿīd al-Aḥwal, Muḥammad, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿAbd Allāh.
He was present at Badr as a polytheist, having been brought out to it unwillingly; he was taken captive, and since he had no money, his uncle al-ʿAbbās ransomed him (1) .
It is narrated that ʿAqīl said to the Prophet ﷺ on the day he was taken captive: Which of their nobles did you kill?
He said: Abū Jahl was killed.
He said: Now the rādī has become clear for you (2) .
Ibn Saʿd said: ʿAqīl set out as an emigrant at the beginning of the year 8, and was present at Mu’tah, then returned and was ill for a time; no mention of him was heard at the conquest of Mecca, nor at Ḥunayn, nor at al-Ṭāʾif.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had granted him at Khaybar one hundred and forty wasqs every year. ⟦1:218⟧
And from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl: that his grandfather found on the day of Mu’tah a ring with images on it, and the Prophet granted it to his father as an extra award (1) .
Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, said:
ʿAqīl came with a needle and said to his wife: Sew your clothes with this.
Then he heard the crier: Let no man steal (2) a needle or anything above it.
So ʿAqīl said to her: I see that your needle has been lost to you (3) .
ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Isḥāq:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAqīl: (O Abū Yazīd! I love you with a twofold love: because of your kinship to me, and because of my uncle’s love for you (4)) .
Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ:
I saw ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib as a very old man whose sharpness had diminished (5) .
They said: He died in the time of Muʿāwiyah, and more of his reports will come later (6) . ⟦1:219⟧

40.t:
Ibn Sharāḥīl - or Sharḥabīl - ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Yazīd ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn ʿĀmir ibn al-Nuʿmān.
The commander, the martyr, the Prophet’s man, the one named in Sūrat al-Aḥzāb, Abū Usāmah al-Kalbī, then al-Muḥammadī, master of the clients (المولى) and the earliest of them to Islam, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the father of his beloved; and the Prophet ﷺ loved only what is good.
Allah the Exalted did not name any Companion (الصحابي) by his name in His Book except Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, and ʿĪsā ibn Maryam (peace be upon him), who will descend as a just ruler and will join this blessed nation in its prayer, its fasting, its pilgrimage, its marriage and all the rulings of the upright religion. Just as Abū al-Qāsim is the master of the prophets, the best of them and their seal, so too ʿĪsā after his descent is the best of this nation without qualification, and he will be their last; none with any good in him will come after him, but rather the sun will rise from its place of setting, and Allah will permit the Hour to draw near (1) .
أخبرنا أبو الفضل بن عساكر، أنبأنا عبد المعز بن محمد، أنبأنا تميم، أنبأنا أبو سعد، أنبأنا ابن حمدان، أنبأنا أبو يعلى الموصلي، حدثنا بندار، حدثنا ⟦1:220⟧ عبد الوهاب الثقفي، حدثنا محمد بن عمرو، عن أبي سلمة (1) ، ويحيى بن عبد الرحمن، عن أسامة بن زيد، عن أبيه، قال:
I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one hot day of the days of Mecca, with him riding me behind him, to one of the stone idols, and we had slaughtered a sheep for it and cooked it. We met Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl.
The Prophet ﷺ said: (O Zayd! Why do I see your people hating you?) .
He said: By Allah, O Muḥammad! That is not for any gain of mine among them (2) , but I went out seeking this religion, until I came to the rabbis of Fadak, and I found them worshipping Allah while associating partners with Him; then I came to the rabbis of Khaybar and found them the same; then I came to the rabbis of Syria and found the same.
So I said: This is not the religion that I seek.
An old man among them said: You are asking about a religion by which we know of no one worshipping Allah, except an old man in al-Ḥīrah.
So I set out until I reached him, and when he saw me he said: Where are you from?
I said: From the people of the House of Allah.
He said: What you are seeking has appeared in your own land; a prophet has been sent, whose star has risen, and all those whom you have seen are in error.
He said: I did not sense anything.
He said: Then the food-cloth was brought near to him, and he said: What is this, O Muḥammad?
He said: A sheep we slaughtered for a stone idol.
He said: I do not eat of what the name of Allah has not been mentioned over.
And we parted. The Messenger of Allah then came to the House and circled it, and I was with him, and between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah; there were two copper idols there: Isāf and Nāʾilah.
When the polytheists circled, they used to touch them.
The Prophet said: (Do not touch them, for they are filth) .
I said to myself: I will surely touch them until I see what he says.
So I touched them, and he said: (O Zayd! Were you not forbidden?) .
He said: Zayd ibn ʿAmr died, and it was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ.
Then the Prophet - ﷺ - said of Zayd: ⟦1:221⟧
(He will be raised as a community by himself (1)) .
In its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is Muḥammad (2), who is not used as proof (يحتج به), and part of it contains clear rejected (المنكر) content.
From al-Ḥasan ibn Usāmah ibn Zayd, who said:
The Prophet ﷺ was ten years older than Zayd.
He said: He was short, very dark-skinned, snub-nosed (3) .
Narrated by: ابن سعد، عن الواقدي، حدثنا محمد بن الحسن بن أسامة، عن أبيه، then Ibn Saʿd said: This is his description in this narration.
It has come by another route: that he was very fair, while his son Usāmah was black, and for that reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased by the words of Mujazziz the physiognomist, when he said: (These feet are some of them from others) (4) . ⟦1:222⟧
Luwayn: حدثنا حديج، عن أبي إسحاق، قال:
Jabalah ibn Ḥārithah was among the clan, and they said to him: Are you older or Zayd?
He said: Zayd is older than me, and I was born before him, and I will tell you:
Our mother was from Ṭayyiʾ, and she died, and we remained in the care of our grandfather; then my two paternal uncles said to our grandfather: We have more right to our brother’s two sons.
He said: Take Jabalah, and leave Zayd.
So they took me and went off with me, and cavalry came from Tihāmah and seized Zayd, and he ended up with Khadījah, who gave him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān (1) : Abū Fazārah narrated to us, saying:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, a boy with a forelock, whom his people had made stand in al-Baṭḥāʾ for sale, and he went to Khadījah.
She said: How much is his price?
He said: (Seven hundred) .
She said: Take seven hundred.
So he bought him and brought him to her, and said: (Were he mine, I would free him) .
She said: Then he is yours. So he freed him (2) . ⟦1:223⟧
And from Sulaymān ibn Yasār and others, who said:
The first to accept Islam was Zayd ibn Ḥārithah.
Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah: عن سالم، عن أبيه، قال:
We used to call Zayd ibn Ḥārithah only Zayd ibn Muḥammad, and then there was revealed: “Call them by the names of their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah” [al-Aḥzāb (1) : 5] .
Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī, said:
Jabalah ibn Ḥārithah informed me, saying:
I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah! Send my brother ⟦1:224⟧ Zayd with me.
He said: (Here he is; if he goes, I will not prevent him) .
Zayd said: No, by Allah, I will never choose anyone over you.
He said: So I saw that my brother’s judgement was better than mine (1) .
ʿAlī ibn Mushir heard it from him.
Ibn Isḥāq and others mentioned him among those who were present at Badr.
Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ said: I fought with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I fought with Zayd ibn Ḥārithah; he used to appoint him commander over us. ⟦1:225⟧
al-Wāqidī: حدثنا محمد بن الحسن بن أسامة، عن أبي الحويرث، قال:
Zayd ibn Ḥārithah went out as commander of seven expeditions (1) .
al-Wāqidī: حدثنا ابن أخي الزهري، عن الزهري، عن عروة، عن عائشة، قالت:
Zayd ibn Ḥārithah arrived back from that mission of his - she means from the expedition of Umm Qirfah - while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in my house.
Zayd knocked (2) at the door, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose, dragging his garment, uncovered - I never saw him uncovered before that, ﷺ - until he embraced him and kissed him, then questioned him, and he told him of the victory Allah had granted (3) .
Ibn Isḥāq: عن يزيد بن عبد الله بن قسيط، عن محمد بن أسامة، عن أبيه، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Zayd ibn Ḥārithah: (O Zayd! You are my client (المولى), and from me, and to me, and the most beloved of the people to me) .
Narrated by: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal in al-Musnad (4) . ⟦1:226⟧
Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar, and Ibn ʿUyaynah: عن عبد الله بن دينار، سمع ابن عمر:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Usāmah as commander over a people, and the people criticised his command.
He said: (If you criticise his command, you have already criticised the command of his father; and by Allah, he was fit for command, and he was among the most beloved of people to me, and this son of his is among the most beloved of people to me after him (1)) .
The wording of Ismāʿīl: (and his son is among the most beloved) .
Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān: عن موسى بن عقبة، عن سالم، عن أبيه: and he mentioned something similar.
In it: (and his father was fit for command, and he was among the most beloved of all people to me) .
Sālim said: I never heard my father narrate this hadith without saying: By Allah, he excepted not even Fāṭimah (2) .
Ibrāhīm ibn Yaḥyā ibn Hāniʾ al-Shajarī (3) : حدثني أبي، عن ابن إسحاق، عن الزهري، عن عروة، عن عائشة، قالت:
Zayd ibn Ḥārithah came to us, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose to him, ⟦1:227⟧ dragging his garment, and kissed his face.
Umm Qirfah had equipped forty riders from her sons and her grandsons to go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in order to fight him, so he sent Zayd against them, and he killed them and killed her, and sent her coat of mail to the Prophet ﷺ, who set it up in Medina between two spears (1) .
Narrated by: المحاملي، عن عبد الله بن شبيب (2) ، عنه.
Part of it was narrated by: الترمذي (3) ، عن البخاري، عن إبراهيم هذا، and he graded it sound (الحسن).
Mujālid: عن الشعبي، عن عائشة، قالت:
Had Zayd been alive, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have appointed him as successor.
Wāʾil ibn Dāwūd: عن البهي، عن عائشة:
The Messenger of Allah never sent Zayd out in an army but that he made him commander over them, and had he lived after him, he would have appointed him as successor (4) .
Recorded by: al-Nasāʾī.
Ibn ʿUmar said: ʿUmar assigned to Usāmah ibn Zayd a larger allowance than he assigned to me, so I spoke to him about ⟦1:228⟧ that, and he said:
He was more beloved to the Messenger of Allah than you, and his father was more beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than your father (1) .
al-Wāqidī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Zayd over the people in the expedition of Mu’tah and placed him ahead of the commanders.
When the two armies met, the commanders were fighting on foot, and Zayd took the banner and fought, and the people fought with him until he was killed by spear-thrusts (may Allah be pleased with him).
He said: The Messenger of Allah prayed over him - that is, made supplication for him - and said: (Ask forgiveness for your brother; he has entered Paradise running) .
Mu’tah took place in Jumādā al-Ūlā, in the year 8, and he was aged 55 (2) .
A group: عن إسماعيل بن أبي خالد، عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي ميسرة، قال:
When the killing of Zayd, Jaʿfar and Ibn Rawāḥah reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he ﷺ stood and mentioned their affair, beginning with Zayd, and said: (O Allah, forgive Zayd, O Allah, forgive Zayd - three times - O Allah, forgive Jaʿfar and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah) (3) .
Ḥammād ibn Zayd, from Khālid ibn Salamah al-Makhzūmī, said:
When the news of the calamity of Zayd and his companions came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to his house after that, and Zayd’s daughter met him and burst into tears in his face.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw her, he wept until he sobbed. Then it was said: What ⟦1:229⟧ is this, O Messenger of Allah?
He said: (The longing of the beloved for the beloved (1)) .
Narrated by: Musaddad and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb from him.
Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid: عن ابن بريدة، عن أبيه:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (I entered Paradise, and a young girl met me.
I said: To whom do you belong?
She said: I belong to Zayd ibn Ḥārithah (2)) .
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is sound (الحسن) (3) .

41.h: 37 - ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Imriʾ al-Qays al-Anṣārī *
41.t:
Ibn Thaʿlabah.
The commander, the fortunate, the martyr, Abū ʿAmr al-Anṣārī, al-Khazrajī, Badrī (البدري), the chief, the poet.
He has: from the Prophet ﷺ and from Bilāl.
Narrating from him: أنس بن مالك، والنعمان بن بشير، and narrating mursal (مرسل) from him: قيس بن أبي ⟦1:230⟧ حازم، وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن، وعطاء بن يسار، وعكرمة، وغيرهم.
He was present at Badr and at al-ʿAqabah.
His patronymic (الكنية) was Abū Muḥammad and Abū Rawāḥah, and he left no descendants.
He was the maternal uncle of al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr.
He was one of the scribes of the Anṣār.
The Prophet ﷺ appointed him as his deputy over Medina in the expedition of Badr al-Mawʿid (1) , and the Prophet (blessings and peace be upon him) sent him on an expedition with thirty riders against Usayr (2) ibn Rizām the Jew at Khaybar, and he killed him.
al-Wāqidī said: The Prophet ﷺ sent him as an appraiser of the crops at Khaybar (3) .
I say: That happened once, and it is possible - though unlikely - that it happened twice.
Qutaybah said: Ibn Rawāḥah and Abū al-Dardāʾ were brothers through their mother.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, in his Musnad: حدثنا عبد الصمد، حدثنا عمارة، عن زياد النميري، عن أنس، قال:
Whenever Ibn Rawāḥah met a man among his companions he would say: Come, let us believe for an hour.
He said it one day to a man, who became angry and went to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
O Messenger of Allah! Do you not see Ibn Rawāḥah turning away from your faith to the faith of an hour?
He said: (May Allah have mercy on Ibn Rawāḥah; he loves the gatherings of which the angels boast) (4) . ⟦1:231⟧
Ḥammād ibn Zayd: حدثنا ثابت، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى:
That ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was delivering a sermon, and heard him saying: (Sit down) .
So he sat down where he was, outside the mosque, until he had finished his sermon, and that reached the Prophet ﷺ, who said: (May Allah increase you in eagerness to obey Allah and His Messenger (1)) .
Part of it is narrated from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah (2) .
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī informed us:
That ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah fainted.
So the Prophet ﷺ came to him and said: (O Allah, if his appointed time has come, ease it for him, and if not, then heal him) .
He felt relief and said: O Messenger of Allah! My mother was saying: Alas, my mountain! Alas, my support! And an angel raised an iron mace, saying: Are you such-and-such? Had I said: Yes, he would have struck me down with it (3) .
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: We would be with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey on a day ⟦1:232⟧ of heat in which there was no one among the people fasting except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah (1) .
Narrated by: غير واحد، عن أم الدرداء، عنه.
Maʿmar: عن ثابت، عن ابن أبي ليلى، قال:
A man married the wife of Ibn Rawāḥah and said to her: Do you know why I married you? So that you would tell me about ʿAbd Allāh’s conduct in his house.
She mentioned something to him that I do not remember, except that she said: When he wanted to leave his house he would pray two rakʿahs, and when he entered he would pray two rakʿahs, never leaving that (2) .
ʿUrwah said: When it was revealed: “And the poets - it is the deviators who follow them” (Qurʾān 26:224), Ibn Rawāḥah said: I am one of them.
Then Allah revealed: “except those who believe and do righteous deeds (3) ” (Qurʾān 26:227).
Ibn Sīrīn said: The poets of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah, Ḥassān ibn Thābit and Kaʿb ibn Mālik.
It was said: When the Prophet ﷺ prepared the three commanders for Mu’tah, he said: (The commander is Zayd, ⟦1:233⟧ and if he is struck down, then Jaʿfar, and if he is struck down, then Ibn Rawāḥah) .
When the two were killed, Ibn Rawāḥah was reluctant to advance, and said:
I swear, O soul, you will go down to it ... willingly, or else you will be made to
For long you have been at ease ... what is it that I see you hate Paradise (1)
Then he fought until he was killed.
Mudrik ibn ʿUmārah said: Ibn Rawāḥah said:
I passed by the mosque of the Prophet ﷺ and sat before him, and he said: (How do you compose poetry when you wish to compose?) .
I said: I consider it, then I speak.
He said: (Then go against the polytheists) .
I had not prepared anything, then I said:
Tell me, O you who are the price of cloaks, since when ... were you at Ṭāriq’s side, or did Muḍar submit to you?
Then I saw that he disliked this, because I had made his people the price of cloaks, so I said:
O Hāshim of goodness, Allah has favoured you ... above creation with a favour that has no change
I have discerned goodness in you, and I know it ... by a discernment in which I differed from what they saw
And had you asked, if you sought help from some of them ... in resolving your matter, they would neither have sheltered nor helped
So may Allah confirm what He has given you of goodness ... as He confirmed Moses, and help like the help they gave
Then the Prophet ﷺ turned to me with his face, delighted, and said: (And you - may Allah confirm you) (2) . ⟦1:234⟧
Ibn Sīrīn said: Ḥassān and Kaʿb used to answer the polytheists in kind with their words, in battles, days of fighting and glorious deeds, while Ibn Rawāḥah used to reproach them with disbelief and ascribe it to them; and when they became Muslims and gained understanding, he was harder on them.
Thābit, from Anas, said:
The Prophet ﷺ entered Mecca in the lesser pilgrimage of the fulfilment, with Ibn Rawāḥah before him, saying:
Clear the way, you sons of the unbelievers, from his path ... today we will strike you over its revelation
A blow that removes heads from their resting places ... and makes the friend forget his friend
ʿUmar said: O Ibn Rawāḥah! In the sanctuary of Allah, and before the Messenger of Allah, you recite poetry?
The Prophet ﷺ said: (Leave him, O ʿUmar, for it is swifter against them than the scattering of arrows) .
And in another wording: (By Him in whose hand is my soul, his words against them are harder than the striking of arrows) (1) .
It was narrated by: معمر، عن الزهري، عن أنس.
al-Tirmidhī (2) said: And it has come in another hadith than this one:
That the Prophet ﷺ entered Mecca in the lesser pilgrimage of the fulfilment, and Kaʿb was saying that.
He said: And this is more authentic (الصحيح) according to some of the people of knowledge, because Ibn Rawāḥah was killed on the day of Mu’tah, ⟦1:235⟧ and the lesser pilgrimage of the fulfilment took place only after that (1) .
I say: No, rather Mu’tah was six months after it, without doubt.
Abū Zurʿah al-Dimashqī said: I said to Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal:
What of the hadith of Anas: The Prophet (blessings and peace be upon him) entered Mecca with Ibn Rawāḥah holding his stirrup (2) ?
He said: It has no basis.
And from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Ibn Rawāḥah: (Get down and urge the riding-camels on) .
He said: O Messenger of Allah! I have abandoned my poetry.
ʿUmar said to him: Listen and obey.
So he got down and said:
By Allah, were it not for Allah we would not have been guided ... nor given charity, nor prayed
And he went on with the rest of it (3) .
Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Qays, said:
Ibn Rawāḥah wept, and his wife wept, and he said: What is the matter with you?
She said: I wept because of your weeping.
He said: I know that I will come to the Fire, ⟦1:236⟧ and I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not (1) .
al-Zuhrī, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār:
That the Prophet ﷺ used to send Ibn Rawāḥah to Khaybar, and he would appraise the crops between him and the Jews.
They collected jewellery from their women and said: This is for you, and go easy on us.
He said: O company of Jews! By Allah, you are among the most hated of Allah’s creation to me, yet that will not make me wrong you; and bribery is illicit gain.
They said: By this the heavens and the earth stand (2) .
And Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن عبد الله - فيما نحسب - عن نافع، عن ابن عمر, similarly.
أخبرنا إسماعيل بن عبد الرحمن، أنبأنا محمد بن المسند بالمزة، أنبأنا ⟦1:237⟧ عبدان بن رزين، حدثنا نصر بن إبراهيم الفقيه، أنبأنا عبد الوهاب بن الحسين، حدثنا الحسين بن محمد بن عبيد، حدثنا محمد بن العباس الزيدي، حدثنا محمد بن حرب، حدثنا محمد بن عياذ، حدثنا عبد العزيز ابن أخي الماجشون:
It has reached us that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah had a slave girl whom he kept secret from his family, and his wife saw him one day alone with her, and said: You have chosen your slave girl over your free wife?
He denied it to her.
She said: If you are truthful, then recite a verse of the Qurʾān.
He said:
I bear witness that the promise of Allah is true ... and that the Fire is the abode of the disbelievers
She said: Give me another verse.
So he said:
And that the Throne is above the water, floating ... and above the Throne is the Lord of the worlds
And noble angels carry it ... angels of the Lord, drawn near
She said: I believe in Allah, and I have denied my own eyes.
Then he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and he laughed and did not change (1) anything for him (2) .
Ibn Wahb: حدثني أسامة بن زيد، أن نافعا حدثه، قال:
Ibn Rawāḥah had a wife whom he was wary of, and he had a slave girl and had relations with her; his wife told him of it, and he said: Glory be to Allah!
She said: Then recite to me, for you are in a state of major impurity.
He said:
I bear witness by the permission of Allah that Muḥammad ... is the Messenger of the One who is above the heavens on high ⟦1:238⟧
And that Abū Yaḥyā and Yaḥyā, both of them ... have a deed from their Lord that is accepted (1)
Both were narrated for Ḥassān.
Sharīk: عن المقدام بن شريح، عن أبيه، عن عائشة:
The Prophet ﷺ used to quote the poetry of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah, and perhaps he would say:
And he will bring you the news who has not been provisioned (2) ...
Ibn Isḥāq: حدثنا محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير، عن عروة، قال:
Then he took the banner - meaning after the killing of his companion.
He said: He turned slightly aside, then advanced with it on his horse, and began to urge himself to dismount, hesitating with it for a while.
He said: And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Ḥazm narrated to me:
That he said at that point:
I swear by Allah, O soul, you will go down to it ... willingly, or else you will be made to
Though the people shout and raise the clamour ... what is it that I see you hate Paradise
For long you have been at ease ... are you anything but a drop of fluid in a worn water-skin
Then he got down and fought until he was killed. ⟦1:239⟧
And he also said:
O soul, if you are not killed you will die ... this is the pool of death, which you have met
And what you wished for has been given to you ... if you do as the two of them did, you will be guided
And if you hold back, you are wretched ... (1)
al-Walīd ibn Muslim said: I heard that they travelled in the region of Maʿān, and were told that the Romans had gathered great forces against them, so Zayd consulted his companions, and they said:
You have trodden the land and frightened (2) its people.
So he turned back, while Ibn Rawāḥah was silent.
He asked him, and he said: We did not march for spoils, but we came out to meet the enemy, and we are not fighting them by number or equipment, and the right course is to march against them.
ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr said:
The Prophet ﷺ said: (If Ibn Rawāḥah is struck down, let the Muslims choose a man) .
Then they marched until they halted at Maʿān, and it reached them that Heraclius had halted at Maʾāb with one hundred thousand of the Romans and one hundred thousand of the Arabized tribes.
Ibn Rawāḥah encouraged the people and said: O my people! By Allah, what you dislike is the very thing you came out for: martyrdom (3) .
And they were three thousand.

42.h: 38 - Kulthūm ibn al-Hidm ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn al-Ḥārith al-Anṣārī *
42.t:
Ibn Zayd ibn ʿUbayd ibn Zayd ibn Mālik ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Mālik ibn al-Aws al-Anṣārī, al-ʿAwfī, elder of the Anṣār, and the one with whom the Prophet ﷺ stayed when he first came to Medina, at Qubāʾ, when he had become old.
The author of al-Ṭabaqāt said: أنبأنا محمد بن عمر، حدثنا مجمع بن يعقوب، عن سعيد بن عبد الرحمن بن رقيش، عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد بن جارية، عن عمه مجمع. (ح) .
وأنبأنا محمد بن عمر، حدثنا ابن أبي سبرة، عن عثمان بن وثاب، عن أبي غطفان، عن ابن عباس، قالا:
Kulthūm ibn al-Hidm was a noble man and advanced in years; he accepted Islam before the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, and when he emigrated, he stayed with him.
He used to hold conversation in the house of Saʿd ibn Khaythamah, which was called: the house of the bachelors (2) . ⟦1:242⟧
For that reason al-Wāqidī said:
It was said: The Prophet ﷺ stayed with Saʿd ibn Khaythamah, and a group of the Emigrants stayed with Kulthūm ibn al-Hidm.
Not long afterwards he died (may Allah be pleased with him), and that was before Badr, and he was a righteous man (1) .

43.h: 39 - Abū Dujānah al-Anṣārī Simāk ibn Kharashah ibn Lawdhān *
43.t:
Ibn ʿAbd Wadd ibn Zayd al-Sāʿidī.
On the day of Uḥud he wore a red headband.
It is said: The Prophet ﷺ established brotherhood between him and ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān.
al-Wāqidī said: Abū Dujānah stood firm on the day of Uḥud with the Prophet ﷺ, and pledged to him to the death.
He was one of those who took part in killing Musaylimah the Liar, and was then martyred on that day (2) .
Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: Abū Dujānah has descendants in Medina and in Baghdad to this day.
Zayd ibn Aslam said: He visited Abū Dujānah while he was ill, and his face was shining.
It was said to him: Why is your face shining?
He said: There is no deed I rely on more than two: I would not speak of what did not concern me, and the other was that my heart was sound toward the Muslims (3) . ⟦1:243⟧
And from Anas ibn Mālik, who said:
On the day of al-Yamāmah Abū Dujānah threw himself into the garden, and his leg was broken, and he fought with his leg broken until he was killed (may Allah be pleased with him (1)) .
It is also said: He is Simāk ibn Aws ibn Kharashah.
Ṣāliḥ ibn Mūsā: عن سهيل بن أبي صالح، عن أبيه، عن أبي هريرة، قال:
When the war laid down its burdens, the Companions (الصحابة) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ boasted of their days, while Ṭalḥah was silent and did not speak, and Simāk ibn Kharashah Abū Dujānah was silent and did not speak (2) .
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said when he saw their silence: (I saw myself on the day of Uḥud, with no created being near me on the earth except Jibrīl on my right and Ṭalḥah on my left (3)) .
The sword of Abū Dujānah was not to be blamed.
That was because the Prophet ﷺ held out that sword until he said: (Who will take this sword with its right?) .
The people held back from it.
Abū Dujānah said: And what is its right, O Messenger of Allah?
He said: (That you fight with it in the way of Allah until Allah grants you victory, or you are killed) .
So he took it on that condition.
Then, before the rout on the day of Uḥud, he went out with his sword drawn, strutting proudly, wearing nothing but a shirt and a red turban with which he had bound his head, and he was reciting verses of rajaz, saying: ⟦1:244⟧
I am a man whom my beloved made a covenant with ... when we were at the foot of the mountain by the date palms
That I would never stay in the fetters for all time ... I strike with the sword of Allah and the Messenger
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (That is a gait (1) that Allah and His Messenger hate, except in a place like (2) this (3)) .
As for the amulet of Abū Dujānah, it is something that is not authentic (الصحيح); I do not know who fabricated it (4) . ⟦1:245⟧

44.h: 40 - Khubayb ibn ʿAdī ibn ʿĀmir ibn Majdaʿah al-Anṣārī *
44.t:
Ibn Jaḥjabā al-Anṣārī, the martyr.
Ibn Saʿd mentioned him, saying: He was present at Uḥud, and he was among those whom the Prophet ﷺ sent with the Banū Liḥyān; when they reached al-Rajīʿ they betrayed them, called for help against them, killed some of them, and captured Khubayb and Zayd ibn al-Dathinah, and sold the two of them in Mecca, and they killed them in retaliation for those of their people whom the Prophet ﷺ had killed, and crucified them at al-Tanʿīm (1) .
Maslamah ibn Jundab said, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Barṣāʾ, who said:
Khubayb was brought and sold in Mecca, and they took him out to the unconsecrated land to kill him, and he said: Let me pray two rakʿahs. Then ⟦1:246⟧ he said: Were it not that you would think it was fear, I would have prayed more. O Allah, count them one by one.
Al-Ḥārith said: And I was present, and by Allah, I did not think that any of us would remain.
Ibn Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar, said:
When ʿAḍal and al-Qārah betrayed Khubayb and his companions at al-Rajīʿ, they brought him and Yazīd ibn al-Dathinah. As for Khubayb, ⟦1:247⟧ Ḥujayr ibn Abī Ihāb bought him for ʿUqbah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir, who was Ḥujayr’s brother through his mother, so that he could kill him in revenge for his father.
When they took him out to kill him, having set up his wooden stake to crucify him, he reached al-Tanʿīm and said:
If you see fit to let me pray two rakʿahs.
They said: Go ahead.
So he prayed, then said: By Allah, were it not that you would think I was prolonging out of fear of death, I would have prayed more.
So he was the first to establish the prayer at the time of execution.
Then they raised him on his stake, and he said: O Allah, count them one by one, and kill them scattered, and leave none of them, O Allah, we have conveyed the message of Your Messenger, so convey to him this morning what has been done to us.
He said: And Muʿāwiyah said: I was among those who attended him, and I saw Abū Sufyān throwing me to the ground out of fear of Khubayb’s supplication.
And they used to say (1) : When a man is cursed and lies down on his side, the supplication slips away from him.
Ibn Isḥāq said: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād narrated to me, from his father, from ʿUqbah ibn al-Ḥārith, who said:
By Allah, I did not kill him, for I was too young for that; but Abū Maysarah al-ʿAbdarī took my hand and put the spear on my hand, then put his hand on my hand, and took it with it, then killed him (2) .
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs: ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān ibn Mawhab, client (المولى) of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir, narrated to me, saying:
Mawhab said: Khubayb said to me - they had placed him with me -: I ask three things of you ⟦1:248⟧ of you: that you give me sweet water to drink, that you keep from me what was slaughtered for the idols, and that you inform me when they intend to kill me (1) .
Ibn Isḥāq: حدثنا ابن أبي نجيح، عن ماوية مولاة حجير، and Khubayb had been imprisoned in her house, and she used to narrate after she accepted Islam, saying:
By Allah, he was imprisoned when I looked in on him from the gap of the door, and in his hand was a cluster of grapes the size of a man’s head, from which he was eating, and I knew of no grape on the earth; then he asked me for a razor to shave himself (2) .

45.h: 41 - Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ ibn Kaʿb al-Anṣārī *
45.t:
Al-Khazrajī, al-Sulamī, al-Madanī, Badrī (البدري), al-ʿAqabī, the killer of Abū Jahl.
Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim said:
From Ibn Isḥāq: Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ ibn Zayd ibn Ḥarām ibn Kaʿb ibn Ghanm ibn Kaʿb ibn Salimah was present at Badr. ⟦1:249⟧
Narrating from him: ابن عباس, and he lived until the late part of the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUmar.
And in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين), by way of Yūsuf ibn al-Mājishūn: أنبأنا صالح بن إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف، عن أبيه، عن جده، قال:
I was standing in the rank on the day of Badr, and I looked, and there I was between two youths of the Anṣār, young in years, and I wished to be between stronger men than they.
One of them nudged me and said: O uncle! Do you know Abū Jahl?
I said: Yes, and what do you want with him?
He said: I was told that he insults the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I see him, my shadow will not leave his shadow until the one of us who is fated to die first dies.
I was amazed at that.
Then the other nudged me and said the same, and it was not long (1) before I looked and saw Abū Jahl moving about among the people, and I said:
Do you not see? That is your man.
He said: They rushed at him with their swords until they killed him, then went back to the Prophet ﷺ and told him.
He said: (Which of you killed him?) .
Each of them said: I killed him.
He said: (Have you wiped your swords?) .
They said: No.
He looked at the two swords and said: (You both killed him) .
And he ruled that his spoils belonged to Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr; the other was Muʿādh ibn ʿAfrāʾ (2) .
And from Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr, who said:
I made Abū Jahl my concern on the day of Badr, and when I was able to, I charged at him and struck him, and cut off his foot at the middle of the shin.
His son ʿIkrimah ibn Abī Jahl struck me on my shoulder and threw off my arm, and it remained hanging by a piece of skin at my side, and the fighting kept me ⟦1:250⟧ from it, so I fought for most of my day, dragging it behind me.
When it pained me, I put my foot on it, then stretched upon it until I threw it off (1) .
This, by Allah, is bravery, not like one who is scratched by an arrow and his heart is cut, and his strength gives way.
Ibn Isḥāq related this story, and said: Then he lived after that until the time of ʿUthmān.
He said: And Muʿawwidh ibn ʿAfrāʾ passed by Abū Jahl, and struck him until he laid him low, and left him with a trace of life in him.
Then Muʿawwidh fought until he was killed, and his brother ʿAwf was killed before him, and they were the two sons of al-Ḥārith ibn Rifāʿah al-Zuraqī.
Then Ibn Masʿūd passed by Abū Jahl, and rebuked him while he had a trace of life, then cut off his head.
أخبرنا أحمد بن سلامة، عن ابن مسعود الجمال، أنبأنا أبو علي، أنا أبو نعيم، حدثنا سليمان بن أحمد، حدثنا أحمد الأبار، حدثنا الهيثم بن خارجة، حدثنا رشدين بن سعد، عن عبد الله بن الوليد التجيبي، عن أبي منصور مولى الأنصار، أنه سمع عمرو بن الجموح يقول:
إنه سمع رسول الله ﷺ يقول: (Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: Truly My friends among My servants, and My beloved among My creation, are those who are remembered by My remembrance, and I am remembered by their remembrance) (2) . ⟦1:251⟧
Rishdīn was alone in narrating it, and he is weak (ضعيف).
This hadith does not belong to the subject of the entry, but to his father.
And they have said that ʿAmr was killed on the day of Uḥud, so how could Abū Manṣūr have heard from him?!

46.h: 42 - Muʿawwidh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ al-Anṣārī al-Sulamī *
46.t: He was present at Badr with his two brothers Muʿādh and Khallād, but Ibn Isḥāq did not mention him, and Allah knows best.

47.h: 43 - Khallād ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ al-Anṣārī **
47.t:
He was present at Badr, and was martyred on the day of Uḥud.
And their father:

48.h: 44 - ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ ibn Zayd ibn Ḥarām al-Sulamī ***
48.t:
Ibn Kaʿb ibn Ghanm ibn Kaʿb (1) ibn Salimah ibn Saʿd ibn ʿAlī ibn Asad ibn Sārdah ibn Tazīd ibn Jusham ibn al-Khazraj al-Anṣārī, al-Sulamī, al-Ghanmī, father of Muʿādh, Muʿawwidh and Khallād, mentioned above, and of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Hind. ⟦1:252⟧
Thābit al-Bunānī narrated, from ʿIkrimah, who said:
Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr came to Medina to teach the people, and ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ sent to him: What is this that you have brought us?
They said: If you wish we will come to you and let you hear the Qurʾān.
He said: Yes.
So he recited the opening part of Sūrat Yūsuf, and ʿAmr said: We have a consultation to make among our people - and he was the chief of the Banū Salimah.
They left, and he went in to Manāf (1) and said: O Manāf! By Allah, you know that the people want no one but you, so do you have any denial?
He said: Then he hung the sword on him, and went out, and his family rose and took the sword.
When he returned, he said: Where is the sword, O Manāf? Woe to you! Even the she-goat defends its rear; by Allah, I see no good in Abū Jaʿār tomorrow.
Then he said to them: I am going to my property, so treat Manāf well.
He went, and they took him, broke him, tied him with a dead dog, and threw him into a well.
When he came, he said: How are you?
They said: Well, our master; Allah has purified our houses of filth.
He said: By Allah, I think you have done badly in succeeding me with Manāf.
They said: There he is, look at him in that well.
He looked down, saw him, and sent for his people, and they came, and he said: Are you not upon what I am upon?
They said: Indeed, you are our master.
He said: Then I call you to witness that I have believed in what was sent down to Muḥammad.
He said: Then on the day of Uḥud, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Rise to a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing) .
He rose, though he was lame, and said: By Allah, I will surely hobble (2) upon it in Paradise.
So he fought until he was killed.
And from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar: that the acceptance of Islam by ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ was delayed, and he had an idol called Manāf, and the young men of the Banū Salimah had believed, and they would wait, until when the night had passed ⟦1:253⟧ they would enter the house of his idol and throw it, head-down, into the foulest pit.
When ʿAmr woke, that distressed him, and he would take it, wash it and perfume it, then they would return to the same deed, until ʿAmr saw how things stood, and became a Muslim.
He composed verses, among them:
By Allah, if you were a god you would not be ... you and a dog in the middle of a well in a rope
Fie on your abode, a god found wanting ... now we have searched you out from the worst of deceptions (1)
He narrated: محمد بن مسلم، عن عمرو بن دينار (ح) ، وفطر بن خليفة، عن حبيب بن أبي ثابت (ح) ، وابن عيينة، عن ابن المنكدر:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (O Banū Salimah! Who is your chief?) .
They said: Al-Jadd ibn Qays, though we consider him stingy.
He said: (And what disease is worse than stinginess? Rather (2) your chief is the white, curly-haired one: ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ (3)) .
al-Wāqidī said: He was not present at Badr, as he was lame, and when they went out on the day of Uḥud his sons prevented him, and said: Allah has excused you.
He went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complaining of them.
He said: (There is no harm if you do not prevent him; perhaps Allah will grant him martyrdom) (4) . ⟦1:254⟧
His wife Hind, the sister of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥarām, said: It is as though I see him, having taken his small shield, saying: O Allah, do not turn me back; and he was killed, he and his son Khallād.
Isrāʾīl: عن سعيد بن مسروق، عن أبي الضحى:
That ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ said to his sons: You prevented me from Paradise on the day of Badr; by Allah, if I live, I will surely enter Paradise.
When the day of Uḥud came, ʿUmar said: I had no concern but him, so I sought him, and there he was in the first detachment (1) .
Mālik said: He and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥarām were shrouded in one shroud.
Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ṣaʿṣaʿah, that it had reached him:
That the flood had damaged the grave of ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ and of Ibn Ḥarām, so they were dug up for them to be moved from their place, and they were found unchanged, as though they had died the day before; and one of them had been wounded and had put his hand on his wound and was buried like that, and his hand was removed from his wound, then released, and it returned as it had been; and between the day of Uḥud and the day they were dug up was forty-six years (2) . ⟦1:255⟧

49.h: 45 - ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy al-Qurashī al-Muṭṭalibī *
49.t:
His mother was from Thaqīf.
He was one of the first forerunners, and he was ten years older than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He emigrated together with his brothers al-Ṭufayl and Ḥuṣayn; he was of medium height, handsome, and held a great station with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He was the one who dueled the chief of the polytheists on the day of Badr; the two exchanged two blows, and each of them incapacitated the other, and ʿAlī and Ḥamzah charged at ʿUtbah and killed him, and carried ʿUbaydah while he had a trace of life; then he died at al-Ṣafrāʾ (1) , in the last ten days of Ramaḍān, in the year 2 (may Allah be pleased with him).
The Prophet ﷺ had appointed him over sixty riders from the Emigrants and tied a banner for him, and it was the first banner tied in Islam; he met Quraysh, led by Abū Sufyān, at Thaniyyat al-Murrah, and that was the first fighting that took place in Islam.
Ibn Isḥāq said it (2) . ⟦1:256⟧

50.h: 46 - Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim al-Hāshimī *
50.t:
Abū Arwā.
His children were: Muḥammad, ʿAbd Allāh, al-Ḥārith, al-ʿAbbās, Umayyah, ʿAbd Shams, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, Arwā the Elder, Hind, Arwā and Ādam.
As for Ādam: he was the one placed with a wet nurse among Hudhayl, and the Banū Layth ibn Bakr killed him in a war that took place among them; he was small, crawling in front of the houses, and a stone struck him and killed him.
The Prophet ﷺ said: (And the first blood I set aside (1) is the blood of the son of Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith (2)) .
It is narrated that he said of him: (Ādam) . He saw in ⟦1:257⟧ the book the blood of the son of Rabīʿah and added an alif, and the apparent explanation is that, because of his youth, his name was not remembered.
It was also said: His name was Tammām ibn Rabīʿah (1) .
They said: Rabīʿah was two years older than his uncle al-ʿAbbās, and at the time of Badr Rabīʿah was absent in Syria.
Ibn Saʿd said: When al-ʿAbbās and Nawfal set out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as emigrants in the days of the Trench, Rabīʿah saw them off as far as al-Abwāʾ, then wanted to return.
They said to him: Where will you return? To the abode of polytheism, fighting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and denying him, when he has become mighty and his companions numerous? Turn back.
So he travelled with them until they all arrived as Muslims.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted Rabīʿah at Khaybar one hundred wasqs every year, and he was present with him at the conquest and at Ḥunayn, and built a house in Medina.
He died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUmar (2) .
It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: (What an excellent servant Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith is, if only he would shorten his hair and hitch up his garment (3)) .
Rabīʿah was a partner of ʿUthmān in trade, and it has come in the hadith of Jābir that is in ⟦1:258⟧ the rites of pilgrimage: (And the first blood I set aside is the blood (1) of the son of Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith) .
He meant the one for whom Rabīʿah was entitled to blood-money (الدية) on account of his son.
It was also said: He died in the year 13.
His mother was Ghuzayyah bint Qays ibn Ṭarīf.

51.h: 47 - ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib al-Hāshimī *
51.t:
The brother of Rabīʿah and Nawfal.
His name was ʿAbd Shams, and it was changed; they narrated that he emigrated shortly before the conquest, and the Prophet ﷺ named him ʿAbd Allāh.
He went out with the Prophet ﷺ on some of his campaigns, and died at al-Ṣafrāʾ, and he shrouded him in his shirt - meaning: the shirt of the Prophet ﷺ.
It has been said that he said of him: (He is fortunate; fortune has reached him (2)) .
Ibn Saʿd reported this thus, without a chain of transmission (إسناد).
And this man has no offspring.

52.h: 48 - Khālid ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayyah al-Umawī **
52.t:
Ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy, ⟦1:259⟧ the great chief, Abū Saʿīd al-Qurashī, al-Umawī, one of the first forerunners.
It is narrated from Umm Khālid bint Khālid, who said:
My father was the fifth in Islam, and he emigrated to the land of Abyssinia and stayed there for more than ten years, and I was born there (1) .
Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUqbah narrated, from Umm Khālid, who said:
My father was the first to write: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him over Ṣanʿāʾ, and that Abū Bakr made him commander over part of the army in the raid on Syria.
Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah said: Our elders informed us:
That Khālid killed a polytheist, then wore his spoils of brocade or silk, and the people looked at him as he was with ʿAmr.
He said: What is it with you that you look? Whoever wishes, let him do the like of Khālid’s deed, then wear his clothing.
It is narrated that when Khālid (may Allah be pleased with him) was martyred, the man who killed him, after he had become a Muslim, said:
Who was this man? For I saw a light of his shining up to the sky.
It was also said: Khālid ibn Saʿīd was handsome and good-looking; he was killed on the day of Ajnādayn, and he emigrated with Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib to Medina at the time of Khaybar, and his daughter mentioned lived long and survived until near the year 90.
His father Abū Uḥayḥah was one of the great men of the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية); he died before the expedition of Badr as a polytheist.
He had several children, among them: ⟦1:260⟧

53.t:
Abū al-Walīd al-Umawī, whose acceptance of Islam was delayed; he was a wealthy merchant who travelled to Syria, and he was the one who gave protection to his cousin ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah when the Prophet ﷺ sent him as an envoy to Mecca; Abān met him, saying:
Come forward and proceed, and fear no one ... the Banū Saʿīd are the mighty ones of the land (1)
Then he became a Muslim on the day of the conquest, or rather before the conquest, and emigrated, and that was because his two brothers, Khālid mentioned above and ʿAmr, when they came from the emigration to Abyssinia to Medina, sent to him calling him to Allah the Exalted, so he hastened and came to Medina as a Muslim.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him in the year 9 over Bahrain.
Then he was martyred, he and his brother Khālid, on the day of Ajnādayn, according to the sound (الصحيح) view.
Abān was the son of the paternal aunt of Abū Jahl.
And their brother:

54.h: 50 - ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ al-Umawī **
54.t:
He had two emigrations: to Abyssinia, then to Medina, and he has a hadith in the Musnad of the Imam Aḥmad (Musnad al-Imām ⟦1:261⟧ Aḥmad).
He was martyred on the day of al-Yarmūk - and it is said: on the day of Ajnādayn - with his two brothers (may Allah be pleased with them).
ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Ashdaq narrated:
That his paternal uncles Khālid, Abān and ʿAmr returned from their posts when the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached them.
Abū Bakr said: No one is more entitled to the work than the officials of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; return to your posts.
They refused and left for Syria, and were killed (may Allah be pleased with them).
